runbooks.diagnosis: Operaton cannot reach PostgreSQL. The JDBC datasource is configured via DB_URL/DB_USERNAME/DB_PASSWORD and the container starts before postgres is ready, or the credentials are wrong.
remediation: Verify postgres is healthy: docker inspect opensme-postgres
Verify DB_USERNAME and DB_PASSWORD match the postgres-init users
Restart the engine after postgres is healthy

runbooks.diagnosis: Operaton JVM heap exhausted. Default JVM heap is too small for large process definitions or high-throughput deployments, or the container memory limit is too low.
remediation: Increase the container memory limit in services/camunda.yml
Set JAVA_OPTS to increase -Xmx (e.g. -Xmx768m) if the default is too low
Check for runaway process instances or infinite loops in BPMN
Restart the engine after adjusting limits

runbooks.diagnosis: Operaton (Spring Boot) failed during startup — usually a missing database table (first-run schema setup), a port conflict on 8080, or a corrupt deployment.
remediation: Check logs for the exact startup phase that failed
If first run, ensure the database schema was created (Operaton auto-creates on first boot)
Verify port 8080 is not already in use by another container
Clear the operaton-data volume only if you accept data loss

runbooks.diagnosis: The REST API is not deployed or the context path is wrong. Operaton serves REST at /engine-rest/engine by default (same as Camunda 7).
remediation: Verify the REST API is enabled (check /operaton/internal/rest/ directory)
Check if the Spring Boot connector is on 8080 and the Traefik rule routes bpm.* correctly

runbooks.diagnosis: The webapps are served at /operaton/app/ (not /camunda/app/). The context path changed from Camunda 7 to Operaton.
remediation: Access /operaton/app/ for the webapps (Cockpit, Tasklist, Admin, Welcome)
Update any bookmarks or links from /camunda/app/ to /operaton/app/
